rationale: Requires both Talarico (TX) and El-Sayed (MI) to win per AP. Late-October polls show Talarico up ~2-4 (Emerson +2, UH +2, TPOR +4) and El-Sayed up ~1-5, both within margin of error; Texas has a strong R lean historically and polls have overstated Democrats there before. Estimating ~0.57 TX and ~0.66 MI with substantial positive correlation gives roughly 0.42. A search result quoted a prediction-market figure for Michigan; it was discarded.

Minnesota has not elected a Republican senator since 2002 and the national environment favors Democrats. Flanagan leads Tafoya by ~3-5 points in averages (RCP +3.4, Pollsmax +4.6), though Cook moved it to Lean D over the fraud scandal and undecideds are high. Strong state lean plus consistent lead gives ~0.88.

ECB hiked 25bp in September to a 2.50% deposit rate; October is a non-projection meeting and late-October OIS/futures pricing points overwhelmingly to a hold, with analysts eyeing December for any further hike. Inflation (3.8% flash) keeps a small hike tail. Search results included prediction-market odds, which were discarded.

Ceasefire currently holding with no confirmed Israel/Iran strikes on each other's territory recently, but NYT/NPR/ABC report US-Israeli plans for resumed strikes on Iran in early November after the Nov 3 midterms, Trump says he is weighing a deal vs. action to 'finish them off', and Netanyahu vows to destroy Iran's nuclear program. Trump has not approved, diplomacy via Pakistan continues, and the Israeli election (Oct 27) may leave a caretaker government. Roughly 40-45% chance of a qualifying Israeli or Iranian strike by Nov 15.

South Carolina is a strongly Republican state (Trump +18 in 2024), but this cycle is unusual: appointed Sen. Darline Graham Nordone leads Annie Andrews by only ~2 in averages, with a D internal showing Andrews +1 and Rasmussen/Trafalgar showing Graham +3-4. Partisan lean and late GOP consolidation favor Graham; a D wave plus close polls keep real upset risk. Search results showed market prices for this race, which were discarded.

Ohio has trended R, but Acton leads Ramaswamy by ~3-4 points in averages (Marist +7, BGSU +6, Fox +2), with Sabato moving it to Lean D on Oct 22 and a favorable midterm environment for the out-party. Ohio polls have historically underestimated Republicans by several points, which is the main argument against, so ~0.64.

Republicans hold 53-47 and keep a 50-50 tie via VP Vance, so Democrats need a net +4. Forecast models cluster at 54-60% for Democrats (DDHQ 56, Call the Map 55, 535 at 54, VoteHub 60, Poliwave 57) with Silver Bulletin at ~75%. Tipping-point races (TX, OH, AK, IA, ME, MI) are all close; Republican control ~0.40.
